title: Man injured after New York shooting involving DHS agents
summary: The shooting happened in the afternoon in the Bronx, with details still emerging. The incident involved the US Department of Homeland Security, the parent agency of US Immigration and Customs…

image.caption: Members of law enforcement have gathered at the scene of the shooting Image: David Dee Delgado/REUTERS

blocks.text: A man was injured after a shooting involving US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) agents, New York City metropolitan police said Thursday.
What do we know so far?
The shooting occurred in the afternoon in the Marble Hill neighborhood of the Bronx, which is one of New York's five boroughs.
Details are still emerging, but the New York Police Department has denied that its personnel were involved in the shooting.
The DHS is the parent agency of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
US President Donald Trump's administration has scaled up ICE raids in major US cities to detain and deport people who are in the US illegally.

blocks.caption: Protesters have also shown up at the scene of the shooting to show their dismay towards ICE Image: Charly Triballeau/AFP

blocks.text: Local media in New York said ICE was involved in the latest shooting in the Bronx, which has sparked protests.
New York Governor Hochul: New Yorkers deserve explanation
New York Governor Kathy Hochul said she was briefed on the incident.

"We expect federal authorities to provide a full and transparent accounting of the circumstances surrounding the incident," Hochul said in a statement posted on X. "New Yorkers deserve to know exactly what happened and why."
DHS has not yet publicly commented on the incident.
Deadly ICE and Border Patrol shootings have drawn controversy during Trump's second term, particularly regarding the training and oversight of the agents.
Minnesota killing spurs backlash over ICE enforcement
An ICE agent killed a 37-year-old US citizen, Renee Good, during their operations in Minnepolis in January, triggering demonstrations not only there but also other US cities.
Later that same month, Alex Pretti, another US citizen, was killed by two US Customs and Border Protection officers agents in Minneapolis following an altercation.
